issues.legal_issue: Concurrent factual findings are not ordinarily disturbed in a special-leave appeal unless exceptional grounds for interference are shown.
material_facts: The trial court and first appellate court found that the claimant provided the purchase consideration and that the property was held in another person's name benami, rather than having been gifted to that person.
Those findings rested on a reasonable appreciation of the evidence, including bank records and testimony, and were affirmed by the High Court.
The appeal challenged those concurrent findings, but no perversity, lack of evidence, or material irregularity affecting them was established.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to interfere with the concurrent finding that the property was held benami and not gifted.
issues.legal_principle: In an appeal under Article 136 of the Constitution, the Court ordinarily does not interfere with a finding of fact that is not perverse or based on no evidence. It may intervene where material circumstances or irregularities affect the finding, justice has failed, or the finding is likely to cause unduly excessive hardship. The Court relied on Babu v. Dy. Director, Prasad v. Govindaswamy, Dhanjibhai v. State of Gujarat, Ganga Bishan v. Jay Narayan, Uday Chand Dutt v. Saibal Sen, and Ram Singh v. Ajay Chawla.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal and concurrent_fact_findings and findings_supported_by_evidence and not material_irregularity_affecting_findings

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The matter is an appeal brought by special leave.
predicates.concurrent_fact_findings: The trial court and the appellate courts reached the same factual finding.
predicates.findings_supported_by_evidence: The courts based their finding on a reasonable appreciation of evidence in the record.
predicates.material_irregularity_affecting_findings: A material irregularity affected the factual findings.

issues.definition: When a special-leave appeal challenges concurrent factual findings supported by evidence and no material irregularity affected them, the findings are not disturbed.

issues.legal_issue: A real owner's action to enforce rights in property held benami is barred when that action remains pending at an appellate stage when the prohibition takes effect, even if the transaction predates the prohibition.
material_facts: The courts below decreed the claimant's action for a declaration of ownership and an injunction after finding that the property had been purchased with the claimant's consideration in another person's name.
The claimant's action was still before the Supreme Court when the prohibition on enforcing rights in benami property took effect.
The property was found to be held benami, and the claimant sought to enforce rights in it as its real owner.
issues.conclusion: The prohibition applied to the pending action and the past benami transaction; the decree could not stand, and the claimant's suit was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(a) and 2(c) of the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988 define benami transactions and property. Section 4(1) bars a suit, claim, or action to enforce a right in property held benami, and section 4(2) bars a defence based on such a right. Although section 3's prohibition on entering benami transactions is not retrospective, section 4 applies to past transactions because it refers broadly to any property held benami and removes the real owner's ability to enforce the claim. The Court treated the Act as declaratory, disqualifying, and retroactive in this respect; it referred to the Law Commission reports, Craies on Statute Law, and Santa Singh v. State of Punjab in addressing statutory construction and legislative intent. It applied the principle ubi jus ibi remedium in explaining that barring the remedy renders the right unenforceable.

predicates.real_owner_recovery_action: A person claiming to be the real owner brought an action to enforce rights in property held in another person's name.
predicates.property_found_held_benami: The property was found to have been transferred to one person for consideration provided by another.
predicates.proceeding_pending_when_prohibition_bega: The action remained pending, including at an appellate stage, when the prohibition on enforcing rights in benami property took effect.

issues.definition: When a real owner seeks recovery of property found to be held benami in an action pending when the prohibition takes effect, the recovery claim is barred.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court hearing an appeal may take account of intervening facts and legislative changes when moulding the relief.
material_facts: The decree under appeal had been made before the relevant legislative change took effect.
The claimant's appeal remained pending before the Supreme Court when the change took effect.
The Supreme Court had seisin of the case on appeal and considered the effect of the intervening change on the relief.
issues.conclusion: The Court was competent to apply the legislative change while deciding the pending appeal, rather than assessing the decree only under the law as it stood when the lower court decided the case.
issues.legal_principle: An appeal is in the nature of a rehearing, and an appellate court may consider facts and events arising after the decree, including legislative changes, when moulding relief. The Court relied on Lachmeshwar v. Keshwar Lal, Shyabuddinsab v. The Gadag-Betgeri Municipal Borough, The King v. The General Commissioner of Income Tax, Mukharjee Official Receiver v. Ramratan Kaur, Dayawati v. Inderjit, Mohanlal Jain v. His Highness Maharaja Shri Man Singh, and Amerjit Kaur v. Pritam Singh. It distinguished Nand Kishore Marwah v. Samundri Devi.

predicates.appeal_pending_after_decree: A party appealed a decree, leaving the case pending before an appellate court.
predicates.intervening_law_changed_before_appeal_de: A legislative change took effect after the decree and before the appellate court decided the appeal.

issues.definition: When an appeal remains pending after a decree and the law changes before the appeal is decided, the appellate court may apply the intervening law.

issues.legal_issue: The rule that no one should suffer from an act of the court does not prevent application of an intervening law merely because an appeal was delayed.
material_facts: The appeal remained pending when the prohibition on enforcing rights in benami property took effect.
The claimant argued that the effect of the intervening law should not be visited on the claimant because of delay in disposing of the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that delay in disposing of the appeal was not an act of the court for purposes of the maxim and did not prevent application of the intervening law.
issues.legal_principle: The maxim actus curiae neminem gravabit means that no one should suffer from an act of the court. The Court held that delay in disposal of an appeal cannot be termed an act of the court for this purpose.

predicates.appeal_pending_during_intervening_law: An appeal remained pending when an intervening legal change took effect.
predicates.appeal_disposal_delayed: The appellate proceeding was not disposed of before the intervening legal change took effect.

issues.definition: When an appeal remains pending during an intervening legal change and its disposal was delayed, that delay does not prevent application of the change.
